A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniMER dataset and UniMERNet research work. Their text, equations, figures and tables support comparison, including v2's appendix. v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset, augmentation and Length-Aware Module ablations, UniMER-Test results, and CROHME/HME100K evaluations in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original recognition experiments, architecture and pretraining ablations, throughput measurements, and appendix studies of encoder and decoder depth.

M1.justification: v1's Length-Aware Module, length embeddings and auxiliary length-prediction loss disappear. v2 introduces Fine-Grained Embedding, convolutional enhancement, removal of shifted-window operations and Squeeze Attention in the decoder, substantially revising the architecture and objective.

E1.justification: The UniMER formula-training sources and four evaluation categories remain. However, v2 newly reports training with 16 million text-image pairs extracted from arXiv papers, extending training coverage from formula recognition to general text-block recognition through pretraining (Table 6).

E2.justification: v2 adds Texify* trained on UniMER-1M with matching augmentation, plus controlled Texify pretraining comparisons. It removes v1 Table 6's comparison against DWAP, DWAP-MSA, BTTR, CoMER, CAN-DWAP, CAN-ABM and SAN. Original Pix2tex/Texify comparisons and qualitative Nougat examples remain.

E3.justification: Reported defaults change from 1024 to 1536 maximum sequence length, 180,000 to 300,000 iterations, and four to eight training GPUs. v2 adds model-size/depth configurations, pretraining controls and throughput testing on an A100 with batch size 128. The separate handwriting evaluation using ExpRate and one-/two-edit tolerances disappears.

E4.justification: The LAM ablation is replaced by component ablations for the revised architecture. v2 adds pretraining ablations, encoder/decoder depth sweeps and dataset symbol-frequency/image-size analyses. Training-source and augmentation ablations remain, with the latter relocated to the appendix and reporting revised results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests. Experimental results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces v1 UniMERNet's CPE/HWE BLEU scores of 0.916/0.921 with UniMERNet-B scores of 0.925/0.895 under revised architecture and training; these are not same-setting gains or losses. v2 adds model-scale, throughput, pretraining and depth results, and removes dedicated handwriting results. Original Pix2tex/Texify scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1's joint language/length objective and piecewise SmoothL1 length-loss definitions disappear (Equations 1 and 3), while cross-entropy is retained as v2 Equation 1. This is a limited revision of formal loss definitions; neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift the central model contribution from sequence-length guidance to fine-detail/local-context encoding and accelerated decoding. Accuracy–speed tradeoffs and configurable model sizes become central claims, while the UniMER dataset contribution and broad real-world recognition claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 explains improvements through length guidance; v2 emphasizes local/global features, redundant shifted windows and decoder computational bottlenecks. New interpretations address depth saturation, Squeeze Attention's accuracy–speed tradeoff, and weaker handwriting benefits from predominantly printed-text pretraining.

D1.justification: The new appendix documents collection-source proportions, perceptual-hash deduplication, fonts, 80–350 DPI rendering, a XeLaTeX template, normalization and augmentation implementation. v2 also specifies model configurations, pretraining-data construction and an additional dataset-access link. Much of the dataset documentation elaborates the existing pipeline rather than establishing changed data.

R1.justification: Most MER related-work coverage remains. v2 adds convolution/Transformer references such as CMT and ConViT, and newer resources including DocGenome, MMSci and OpenDataLab. The LAM comparison with counting-aware recognition and several backbone/handwriting references disappear, but the overall research framing remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset description, methods and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. CNN and Transformer related-work subsections are merged, and augmentation material moves into a new appendix alongside expanded dataset documentation and architecture analyses.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, replaces the architecture diagram, restyles retained figures and expands comparison tables with parameter counts and throughput. New dataset-distribution plots, an augmentation gallery, a rendering listing and additional ablation tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence separating architecture benefits from training-data effects through matched-data Texify comparisons and shared-pretraining controls (Tables 5–6). Component/depth studies and throughput measurements support its revised claims, while the appendix resolves important gaps in dataset-construction documentation. Removing the specialist handwriting comparison weakens that aspect of evaluation, but the improvements in experimental attribution and reproducibility outweigh this loss.
